_README: RECONCILED — Stage 2 scoped fact-build for 3 domains (health/pharmacy/hospital billing, Balearic ferries, public holidays/closures). Panel: claude + deepseek + grok. This SUPERSEDES the mechanical reconcile.mjs pass in this same folder's git history: that script does exact-string comparison, which flagged 22/23 fields as 'disputed' purely because three independently-written paragraphs are never byte-identical, even when substantively agreeing. This file is the human-judgment merge — substantively agreeing fields are synthesized into one clean value; only the 5 fields with a REAL factual conflict are left status:'disputed' pending your ruling (see disputes.md, hard-capped at 5 per Stage 2 doctrine).

locale.money_framing: express costs in USD with EUR equivalents

_fact_field_shape: Every FACT uses: { value, source_url, status (verified|agreed_stable|verify_recommended|serve_live|disputed), notes }. 'verified' reserved for a source Claude itself opened and checked — a source URL a PANEL MEMBER claims to have used is NOT independently verified and stays verify_recommended until someone actually opens it.

prescription_medication_rules.value: Personal prescription medication may be brought into Spain for up to a 3-month supply, in original pharmacy-labeled packaging (name must match the passport). Carry the original US prescription or a signed doctor's letter (name, condition, dosage) — a Spanish pharmacy cannot fill a US prescription, so a local doctor must issue a new one for any refill beyond that. Do NOT mail refills from the US to a Spanish address — customs prohibits receiving medication by mail and will confiscate it.
prescription_medication_rules.notes: RESOLVED 2026-09-06 (was DISPUTE 1) — the 3-month figure is independently corroborated: BU Madrid's institutional page states it directly for general prescriptions, and the official AEMPS page (fetched directly, see controlled_substances_note) states the same 3-month cap for the controlled-substances permit, so it converges from two angles. Kept 'verify_recommended' rather than 'verified' because BU Madrid is institutional, not a Spanish government page — the general (non-controlled) case has not been confirmed on an official .gob.es page directly.

controlled_substances_note.value: Narcotic/psychotropic medications (ADHD stimulants like Adderall/Ritalin/Concerta, opioids like Oxycodone/Tramadol/Codeine, benzodiazepines like Xanax/Valium) require a formal traveler's authorization from AEMPS (Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios) BEFORE departure — you cannot simply cross the border with them. Apply by email (an aemps.gob.es address — sources give slightly different variants: 'Estupefacientes@aemps.es' and 'estupefacientes_viajeros@aemps.es'; confirm the current one on the live AEMPS page before publishing) at least 10 days ahead, attaching: a PDF passport copy, flight itinerary, the US prescription, and a doctor's certificate detailing daily dose and total quantity needed for the trip. The permit/quantity is capped at roughly a 3-month supply.
controlled_substances_note.notes: RESOLVED 2026-09-06 (was DISPUTE 2) — fetched aemps.gob.es directly: it confirms the permit/certificate scheme ('Certificados y permisos para el transporte de medicamentos estupefacientes y psicótropos por viajeros en tratamiento médico') and the 3-month quantity cap in its own Spanish text. BU Madrid's institutional page independently corroborates the email/10-day/document-list operational detail. The exact email address has a minor variant across sources — flagged in _open_questions, not treated as settled.

customs_declaration_threshold.value: No fixed value/quantity threshold found; medicines for personal use are generally exempt from ordinary traveler duty-free limits as long as the quantity plausibly matches a personal treatment course (i.e. within the ~3-month cap above). Declare if asked, or for larger quantities.
customs_declaration_threshold.notes: one source (grok) cited agenciatributaria.gob.es for this — not independently opened, treat as a lead not a confirmation

official_source_url.notes: Confirmed live 2026-09-06 by direct fetch — this IS the correct official AEMPS page for the traveler medication scheme.

farmacia_identification.value: Look for the illuminated green cross ('cruz verde') sign — pharmacies are marked 'Farmacia' and are ubiquitous even in small neighborhoods.

farmacia_de_guardia.value: A rotating 24-hour duty-pharmacy system keeps at least one pharmacy open per zone every night, Sunday, and holiday; every closed pharmacy posts the address of the current on-duty one in its window.
farmacia_de_guardia.notes: Panel named THREE different lookup tools (farmaciasdeguardia.com, farmaguia.net, and the Col·legi de Farmacèutics de Barcelona/COFB site) — confirm which is actually live and current before publishing a URL; see _open_questions.

otc_vs_prescription_differences.value: Nearly all medicines are sold only in pharmacies, never supermarkets. Paracetamol 1g and lower-dose ibuprofen (≤400mg) are OTC; higher-dose ibuprofen (600mg), codeine combinations, and most antibiotics need a Spanish prescription. Metamizol/Nolotil is a common OTC-level Spanish painkiller with no US equivalent. Emergency contraception is OTC. Ask the pharmacist by symptom, not US brand name — US brand names generally don't exist there.
otc_vs_prescription_differences.notes: specific dosage thresholds supplied by grok only — corroborated in shape by deepseek, not independently verified

pharmacist_role.value: Spanish pharmacists are trained to assess and treat minor ailments directly at the counter (colds, mild pain, minor wounds, digestive issues) without a doctor visit, and will direct you to a clinic when something needs more.

private_clinic_access.value: Walk-in private clinics and tourist-oriented medical centers (e.g. Creu Blanca, Quirónsalud) are widely available in Barcelona; same-day, hours-not-days wait. Typical self-pay consultation roughly €60-200 depending on the clinic and whether tests are added; many accept cards and speak English.
private_clinic_access.notes: price range is an unverified panel estimate, serve_live in spirit — refresh before publishing

public_hospital_er_access.value: Public hospital urgencias (ER) triages and treats anyone regardless of nationality or ability to pay — emergency stabilization cannot legally be refused, and no insurance card is demanded at the door. A US tourist is billed afterward for care once it's no longer classified as immediate emergency stabilization. Non-urgent waits can run several hours in peak season.

when_to_choose_which.value: Pharmacy first for anything minor (cold, mild rash, small cut). A private clinic for a non-urgent issue that still needs a doctor — faster, English more likely, bills go straight to travel insurance. Public ER, or calling 112 directly, only for a true emergency (chest pain, difficulty breathing, major trauma); 112 operators speak English.

billing_model_public.value: Non-EU tourists are generally billed for public hospital care beyond emergency stabilization; the invoice may be handed over at discharge or mailed afterward, depending on the hospital. One source flagged that some facilities route billing through intermediaries that can inflate the final charge — worth a caution line in the article, not yet independently corroborated.

billing_model_private.value: Private clinics/hospitals typically require a card guarantee or upfront payment (partial or full) before non-emergency treatment, then issue an itemized invoice for the patient to submit to their own travel insurer for reimbursement.

typical_costs.value: Unverified, rough panel estimates only — NOT to be published as fixed prices: private consultation roughly €60-200; public ER visit for a non-EU tourist roughly €100-300 before tests/imaging; overnight stay materially more; ambulance billed separately. Refresh/qualify at write time.

travel_insurance_necessity.value: Effectively essential for this audience — US Medicare/Medicaid and most US health plans do not cover care in Spain. Without insurance, the tourist pays out of pocket and seeks reimbursement after the fact, if at all.

what_to_keep_for_reimbursement.value: Itemized invoice (factura / factura desglosada), the medical report (informe médico), a discharge summary if hospitalized, any prescriptions issued, and every payment receipt — a US insurer's claim needs all of it, ideally with an English or bilingual copy requested before leaving the facility.

operators.notes: RESOLVED 2026-09-06 (was DISPUTE 3) — Baleària + Trasmediterránea confirmed by all 3 panel sources; GNV was named by grok only, confirmed by fetching gnv.it directly, which lists Barcelona-Palma de Mallorca, Barcelona-Ibiza, and Barcelona-Mahón (Menorca) among its routes. All three operators are real for this corridor.

port_terminal.value: Port de Barcelona has multiple ferry terminals; which one and which metro line serves it varies by operator and sometimes by sailing — confirm the terminal printed on your actual ticket rather than assuming. Drassanes (metro L3) is the terminal-area metro stop most consistently named across sources.
port_terminal.notes: Sources conflicted on metro line (L2 vs L3) and on which operator uses which named terminal (Moll de Barcelona / Moll de Sant Bertran / Moll Adossat) — flagged in _open_questions as a live-check item, not elevated to a top-5 dispute since it's routine serve_live logistics, not a factual/legal split

to_palma_mallorca.value: A conventional overnight/day ferry of roughly 6-8.5 hours is the mainstay; a faster option in the roughly 2.5-3.5 hour range exists on at least some sailings/operators. Price ranges quoted by the panel varied too widely to state a number here.
to_palma_mallorca.notes: durations converge roughly; exact current timetable and fare must be checked live before writing

to_ibiza.value: Mostly overnight conventional ferries in the roughly 8-10 hour range; a same-day fast option was not confidently confirmed by all sources.

to_menorca.value: A direct Barcelona-Mahón route exists (confirmed listed on GNV's own site alongside Palma and Ibiza), though it's more seasonal than the Mallorca/Ibiza legs; roughly 7-10 hours conventional or ~3.5-5.5 hours fast where a fast option runs, mostly in summer.
to_menorca.notes: direct-vs-routed corrected 2026-09-06 after confirming GNV lists Barcelona-Mahón directly; exact current schedule/operator mix still serve_live

fast_vs_slow_tradeoffs.value: Fast ferry: saves a travel day, costs more, rougher in bad weather, fewer cabin options. Conventional overnight ferry: cheaper, a cabin lets you sleep through the crossing and arrive rested, better for bringing a car or traveling on a budget. Choose fast only when the schedule and price both actually work — it isn't offered on every route or every day.

booking_advice.value: Book weeks to months ahead for July-August sailings, earlier still for a cabin or a car space; foot passengers have more last-minute flexibility. Compare the operator's own site (e.g. balearia.com, trasmediterranea.es) against an aggregator (e.g. Direct Ferries) since fares and terms aren't always mirrored — the operator's own site is usually clearest on changes/cancellation terms.

typical_causes.value: Adverse weather — high wind and rough sea state exceeding the vessel's safe operating limits — is the dominant cause; mechanical/operational issues are less common but happen.

passenger_rights.value: EU Regulation (EC) No 1177/2010 on the rights of passengers traveling by sea governs cancellations/delays: a cancellation or a departure delay beyond a threshold generally entitles the passenger to a choice of full refund or free re-routing under comparable conditions, plus care obligations (meals/refreshments, and accommodation for an overnight wait). Cash compensation for a late arrival is more limited and generally does NOT apply when the cause is 'extraordinary circumstances' such as weather — exact compensation percentages/thresholds were reported inconsistently across sources and are not repeated here as firm numbers.
passenger_rights.notes: the regulation and its general shape are corroborated by all 3; specific compensation percentages (one source: 25%/50%) are NOT independently confirmed — do not publish a number without checking the regulation text directly

operator_rebooking_practice.value: Operators generally offer rebooking on the next available sailing or a full refund; contact the carrier promptly and keep records/original tickets.

travel_insurance_interaction.value: A standard policy's 'trip interruption' or 'transport disruption' clause is what would cover extra costs from a cancelled ferry (missed connection, extra hotel night); plain trip-cancellation coverage usually does not. Weather-caused cancellations are more often covered than operator-caused ones (e.g. insolvency) — check the specific policy wording.

national_holidays.notes: IDENTICAL set named by all 3 sources, only wording/date-format differed — reconcile.mjs flagged this as a 'dispute' in error (exact-string match); genuinely agreed. Confirm against the official BOE/Ajuntament calendar for the actual travel year before publishing.

value.name: Diada Nacional de Catalunya (National Day of Catalonia)
Sant Esteve / St Stephen's Day (Boxing Day)

catalonia_regional_holidays.notes: RESOLVED 2026-09-06 (was DISPUTE 4) — fetched publicholidays.es's 2026 Catalonia calendar directly: Sant Jordi (Apr 23) is explicitly NOT listed as an official public holiday, confirming claude+grok over deepseek (deepseek had conflated the cultural book-and-rose festival with a legal day off). Easter Monday IS confirmed as a genuine Catalonia-specific regional holiday. Government sites (govern.cat, ajuntament.barcelona.cat) blocked automated fetches (403/418) — this third-party holiday-calendar aggregator was used instead; re-verify against the official Generalitat DOGC/BOE publication before the travel year in question.

value.name: Whit Monday / Pentecost Monday (Segona Pasqua / Dilluns de Pasqua Granada)
value.typical_date: May 25, 2026 — CHANGES ANNUALLY, tied to Easter

barcelona_local_holidays.notes: RESOLVED 2026-09-06 (was DISPUTE 5) — gremicat.es confirms Barcelona's two 2026 local-holiday DATES directly (May 25 and Sep 24); May 25, 2026 checks out astronomically as Whit Monday (Easter 2026 = Apr 5 -> Pentecost Sun = May 24 -> Whit Mon = May 25), confirming grok over deepseek's Santa Eulàlia (Feb 12) claim. IMPORTANT: Barcelona's city council re-picks its 2 local holidays EVERY YEAR (Whit Monday moves with Easter, and the council could pick a different second day entirely in another year) — this value is 2026-specific, do not carry it forward to future-year articles without re-checking. ajuntament.barcelona.cat (primary source) blocked automated fetches (418) — gremicat.es used as a third-party check instead.

what_typically_closes.value: On the bigger national/religious holidays: most independent shops close; malls, big chains, and tourist-zone shops mostly stay open (sometimes on reduced hours); restaurants in residential neighborhoods often close while tourist-area restaurants/bars/cafés mostly stay open; banks and government offices close; museums commonly switch to a Sunday-style or special holiday schedule rather than closing outright — check individually; public transport runs its reduced Sunday/holiday timetable ('horario festivo'); pharmacies keep running via the rotating guardia system.
what_typically_closes.notes: All 3 sources substantively agree — reconcile.mjs flagged this as disputed only due to wording differences

august_shutdown_specifics.value: Many small, family-run shops and neighborhood restaurants post 'cerrado por vacaciones' and close for roughly 1-3 weeks sometime in July-August, commonly clustered around the August 15 Assumption holiday, with no single fixed citywide date. Tourist-core areas (Gothic Quarter, El Born, Barceloneta, Las Ramblas), hotels, major attractions, and chains stay open throughout; supermarkets and essential services continue, sometimes on reduced hours; museums generally keep operating though may be short-staffed.
august_shutdown_specifics.notes: All 3 sources substantively agree on the shape; no source gave a hard percentage of businesses affected — stays qualitative, feeds barcelona-august-shutdown

advance_planning_note.value: Book restaurant reservations further ahead around national/regional holidays and especially in August; check individual attraction/museum hours for the exact date rather than assuming normal hours; confirm ferry and train schedules since some reduce frequency; use the official pharmacy-guardia finder rather than assuming a specific pharmacy is open.
